correctness.rationale: For u,v>0, x=log u,y=log v, E=λ^(−1)f(x)+λ f(y), f(z)=e^z−z−1 is proper strictly convex; each E>0 is a compact regular Hamiltonian oval. Under λ=cE, M=λ E=cE² and g(y)=1−c f(y) on [y−,y+] where f(y±)=1/c, the inverse x branches solve f(x)=Mg(y). Exact original-time branch densities λd±(Mg(y))dy use d−=1/(1−e^s−),d+=1/(e^s+−1). Near simple endpoint zeros of g, d±=O(h^(−1/2)); for large h, d−−1 decays exponentially while d+=O(h^(−1)). Hence integrals of d−−1 and d+ are O(1/M) and O(log M/M), yielding T=cE(y+−y−)+O_c(log E/E). Exact negative-branch identity |−s−(h)−h|≤1 gives uniform first-coordinate fold error 1/M; small positive-branch mass and bounded support yield W1 original-time occupancy to law (1−cf(Z),Z) with Z uniform [y−,y+] at O_c(log E/E²). The supplied check_lv_crossover.py reconstructs LambertW inverse branches and quadratures for finite c/E (inspected, not relied on as proof); analytical estimates justify infinite limit.
